title: Present Tense Verb Classes (-am, -em, -im)
subtitle: Master the three primary present-tense thematic vowel patterns in Slovenian
keyPoint: Slovenian verbs conjugate in the present tense by attaching person endings to stems defined by three primary thematic vowels: -a-, -e-, or -i-.

mistakes.note: Never use the infinitive (-ti) when conjugating for a specific subject; replace it with the person ending.
Subject pronouns like 'oni' are usually omitted in natural Slovenian unless needed for emphasis or contrast.
The verb pisati belongs to the -em class and undergoes a consonant mutation (s -> š).

quiz.question: How do you say 'I speak' using the verb 'govoriti'?
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular (jaz) ending for the -im class is -im: 'govorim'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Mi ___ v Ljubljani.' (živeti - to live)
quiz.explanation: The first-person plural (mi) ending across all present tense classes ends in -mo: 'živimo'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Kaj ti ___?' (delati - to do/work)
quiz.explanation: The second-person singular (ti) ending is -š: 'delaš'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Otroci ___ sok.' (piti - to drink, 3rd pl.)
quiz.explanation: Third-person plural (oni/otroci) for this class takes the ending -jo: 'pijejo'.

tip: To guess the class, look up the 1st person singular form; dictionaries list infinitives alongside 'delam', 'pišem', or 'govorim'.

title: The Dual Number (Dvojina) in Nouns and Verbs
subtitle: Discover Slovenian's rare and distinctive grammatical number for pairs
keyPoint: Whenever exactly two people or things are involved, Slovenian uses special dual forms for nouns, pronouns, and verbs instead of plural.

useCases.label: Two mixed or male speakers ('we two')

mistakes.note: 'Smo' is plural (3+ people); for two people speaking, use the dual verb form 'sva'.
Feminine dual uses the number 'dve' and takes the ending -i ('mizi'), not the masculine 'dva'.
Both the noun and the verb must be in dual ('dva avtomobila sta'), not plural.

quiz.question: Which verb form completes the sentence: 'Midva ___ prijatelja.' (We two are friends)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person dual form of 'biti' (to be) for 'midva/medve' is 'sva'.

quiz.question: Select the correct dual form for 'two apples' (jabolko is neuter):
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns in the dual nominative take the numeral 'dve' and suffix -i: 'dve jabolki'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Vidva ___ dobro slovensko.' (govoriti - you two speak)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person dual ending for verbs is -ta: 'govorita'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'two students (masculine)' in the nominative dual?
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns use 'dva' and add the dual suffix -a: 'dva študenta'.

tip: Paired body parts like 'oči' (eyes) or 'roki' (hands) naturally use dual forms without even needing the numeral 'dve'.

title: Accusative Case and Animacy Distinction
subtitle: Direct objects and the crucial split between living beings and inanimate things
keyPoint: In the masculine accusative singular, animate nouns (people and animals) add -a, while inanimate objects remain identical to the nominative.

mistakes.note: Because 'brat' is a living person (masculine animate), its accusative singular must take -a.
An 'avtomobil' is inanimate; its accusative singular remains unchanged from nominative.
Feminine nouns ending in -a must switch to -o in the accusative singular.

quiz.question: Choose the correct accusative form: 'Poznam tega ___.' (človek - man/person)
quiz.explanation: Since 'človek' is masculine animate, it takes the accusative suffix -a: 'človeka'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Kupujem nov ___.' (stol - chair, inanimate)
quiz.explanation: Inanimate masculine objects maintain their nominative form in the accusative: 'stol'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Iščem svojo ___.' (mačka - cat, fem.)
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -a take -o in the accusative singular: 'mačko'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly treats the animate masculine direct object?
quiz.explanation: 'Brat' is a person (animate masculine), so 'Imam brata' correctly receives the -a ending.

tip: Ask yourself: 'Does it breathe?' If it is a male human or animal, add -a in the singular accusative.

title: Locative Case with 'pri', 'v', and 'na'
subtitle: Expressing static location using the fifth case in Slovenian
keyPoint: The locative case in Slovenian never stands alone and expresses stationary location when paired with prepositions like v (in), na (on), and pri (at/by).

mistakes.note: Stationary location requires the locative case ending (-i for feminine nouns), not nominative.
Offices use preposition 'v' (inside), and 'pisarna' takes the locative suffix -i.
Masculine nouns after 'pri' take the locative ending -u: 'pri zdravniku'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ali živiš v ___?' (Ljubljana)
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -a take -i in the locative singular: 'v Ljubljani'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Telefon je na ___.' (miza - table)
quiz.explanation: After 'na' expressing static location, feminine 'miza' takes the locative ending -i: 'na mizi'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Peter je zdaj pri ___.' (zdravnik - doctor)
quiz.explanation: Masculine singular nouns take -u in the locative: 'pri zdravniku'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Vlak stoji na ___.' (peron - platform)
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns in the locative singular take -u: 'na peronu'.

tip: Remember the golden pair: masculine & neuter locative singular end in -u, while feminine singular ends in -i.

title: Instrumental Case with 's/z'
subtitle: Express accompaniment and learn the phonetic rule for choosing 's' versus 'z'
keyPoint: The instrumental case with 's' or 'z' expresses company or accompaniment, using 's' before voiceless consonants (c, č, f, h, k, p, s, š, t) and 'z' everywhere else.

cells: Before c, č, f, h, k, p, s, š, t ('Ta Suhi Škafec Pušča')
Before b, d, g, j, l, m, n, r, v, z, ž
Before all vowels (a, e, i, o, u)

useCases.label: Instrument or accompaniment with feminine nouns

mistakes.note: Use 's' instead of 'z' before voiceless consonants like 'p'.
The consonant 'm' is voiced, so it requires the preposition 'z', not 's'.
Two mistakes: 's' must be used before 's', and feminine instrumental singular takes the ending -o.

quiz.question: Choose the correct preposition and ending: 'Grem na kavo ___.' (kolega - masc. colleague)
quiz.explanation: 'K' is voiceless, demanding 's', and masculine instrumental singular ends in -om: 's kolegom'.

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly expresses 'with milk' (mleko - neuter)?
quiz.explanation: 'M' is voiced, so use 'z', and neuter nouns take -om in the instrumental: 'z mlekom'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Pogovarjam se ___.' (brata - brother/brat)
quiz.explanation: 'B' is a voiced consonant, so we use 'z', and the masculine instrumental singular ending is -om: 'z bratom'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Jem kruh ___ maslom.'
quiz.explanation: The noun 'maslom' begins with the voiced consonant 'm', requiring the preposition 'z'.

tip: Remember the classic mnemonic sentence 'Ta suhi škafec pušča'—its consonants (t, s, h, š, k, f, c, p, č) are exactly those that require 's' instead of 'z'!

title: Wackernagel Clitic Ordering Basics
subtitle: Positioning unstressed pronouns and auxiliary verbs strictly in the second slot
keyPoint: Slovenian clitics (unstressed pronouns, auxiliary verbs, and the reflexive marker 'se') must occupy the second syntactic slot in a clause.

mistakes.note: Clitics cannot initiate an independent declarative clause; an element must precede them.
Clitics must follow the first constituent directly rather than floating toward the middle.
Auxiliary and pronoun clitics cluster together right after the first constituent.

quiz.question: Yesterday I went to school: 'Včeraj ___ šel v šolo.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary clitic 'sem' correctly fills the second syntactic position after the adverb 'Včeraj'.

quiz.question: They are washing themselves: 'Otroci ___ umivajo.'
quiz.explanation: 'Se' is the reflexive clitic placed immediately after the subject constituent 'Otroci'.

quiz.question: Where does the clitic 'ga' belong in 'Marko ___ vidi vsak dan.'?
quiz.explanation: The short accusative pronoun clitic 'ga' occupies the second position directly after the first element 'Marko'.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly ordered sentence:
quiz.explanation: 'Včeraj sem kupil kruh' adheres strictly to the Wackernagel rule placing 'sem' right after 'Včeraj'.

tip: Treat the first constituent as a single grammatical phrase—whether it is one word ('Danes') or five words ('Moj zelo dober prijatelj')—the clitic group snaps directly after it.

title: Past Tense Formation with the L-Participle
subtitle: Combining present auxiliary 'biti' with the agreement-marked active participle
keyPoint: The Slovenian past tense pairs the present tense of 'biti' (sem, si, je...) with an active L-participle that inflects for gender and number.

examples.en: Midva sva jedla kosilo ob dveh.

mistakes.note: Slovenian requires the auxiliary verb 'sem/si/je...'; the L-participle alone cannot form the standard past tense.
The L-participle must agree in gender with the subject (feminine -la for Ana).
First person dual requires the auxiliary 'sva', not the second/third person dual 'sta'.

quiz.question: Female speaker saying 'I lived in Ljubljana': 'Jaz ___ v Ljubljani.'
quiz.explanation: A female speaker uses first-person singular auxiliary 'sem' with feminine singular participle 'živela'.

quiz.question: Two boys 'slept': 'Fanta ___.'
quiz.explanation: Dual masculine subject requires 3rd person dual auxiliary 'sta' and masculine dual participle ending '-a' (spala).

quiz.question: Choose the form for 'We (plural, all female) read': 'Mi/Me ___ knjige.'
quiz.explanation: First-person plural auxiliary is 'smo' and the feminine plural participle ending is '-e' (brale).

quiz.question: Third-person singular masculine: 'Peter ___ kavo.'
quiz.explanation: Peter (he) takes 3rd person singular auxiliary 'je' and masculine ending '-l' (pil).

tip: Pay close attention to dual endings on the participle: masculine dual ends in '-a' (fanta sta tekla), while feminine dual ends in '-i' (dekleti sta tekli).

title: Genitive of Negation and Absence
subtitle: Switching direct objects from accusative to genitive under verbal negation
keyPoint: When an affirmative transitive verb takes an accusative direct object, negating the verb triggers the genitive case on that object.

cells: I do not have a new phone.

examples.en: Peter pije vodo, toda jaz ne pijem vode.

mistakes.note: Negating 'imeti' requires the direct object in the genitive case, not accusative.
The direct object 'kava' shifts from accusative 'kavo' to genitive 'kave' when negated.
Existential absence expressed by 'ni' requires the subject of absence to take the genitive.

quiz.question: I do not have a sister: 'Nimam ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Sestra' in feminine genitive singular takes the '-e' ending: 'sestre'.

quiz.question: He does not understand the problem: 'Ne razume ___.'
quiz.explanation: Masculine inanimate noun 'problem' takes the genitive singular ending '-a'.

quiz.question: There is no milk in the fridge: 'V hladilniku ni ___.'
quiz.explanation: Absence with 'ni' demands genitive; neuter noun 'mleko' becomes 'mleka'.

quiz.question: We did not see that movie: 'Nismo videli ___ filma.'
quiz.explanation: Genitive masculine singular for 'tisti film' is 'tistega filma'.

tip: Whenever you formulate a sentence with 'ne' or 'ni' followed by an object or indicating someone's absence, instinctively reach for the genitive case ending.

title: Future Tense with 'bom' + L-Participle
subtitle: Expressing forthcoming events with the future auxiliary and active participle
keyPoint: The future tense in Slovenian is built by combining the future-tense auxiliary stem 'bo-' with the gender- and number-agreeing L-participle.

examples.en: V soboto bova šla na izlet.

mistakes.note: Slovenian future tense takes the L-participle, never the infinitive (-ti).
Be sure the participle matches gender and number ('šli' for masculine/mixed plural).
Auxiliary must match 3rd person singular ('bo'), not 1st person ('bom').

quiz.question: Tomorrow I (female) will work: 'Jutri ___.'
quiz.explanation: First-person singular future is 'bom' and feminine singular participle is 'delala'.

quiz.question: When will you (singular informal) call me: 'Kdaj me ___ poklical?'
quiz.explanation: 'Boš' is the second-person singular future auxiliary form of biti.

quiz.question: The students (masculine plural) will learn: 'Študenti se ___ učili.'
quiz.explanation: Third-person plural auxiliary form is 'bodo' (or colloquial 'bojo').

quiz.question: We two (male speaker + friend) will swim: 'Midva ___ plavala.'
quiz.explanation: 'Bova' is the first-person dual future auxiliary.

tip: Unlike English ('will do') or German ('werden machen'), Slovenian never uses an infinitive with 'bom'. Always pair 'bom' with the exact same '-l' participle you learned for the past tense.

title: Dative Case and Clitic Pronoun Chains
subtitle: Marking indirect recipients and ordering clitic pronouns: Dative precedes Accusative
keyPoint: Indirect objects take the dative case, and when unstressed pronouns cluster together, the dative clitic always precedes the accusative clitic.

cells: On mi je dal... (He gave me...)
Dal mu ga je. (He gave him it.)

examples.en: Knjigo imam in jo bom dal Petru.
Oče mi jo je podaril za rojstni dan.

mistakes.note: Dative clitics (mu) must precede accusative clitics (ga) in the pronoun cluster.
Recipients in Slovenian use the bare dative case ('prijatelju'), not preposition 'za'.
Verbs of communicating/telling take the recipient in the dative case (njemu/mu).

quiz.question: He gave it (feminine, 'jo') to me ('mi'): 'On ___ je podaril.'
quiz.explanation: Dative clitics strictly precede accusative clitics: 'mi' (to me, dat.) + 'jo' (her/it, acc.).

quiz.question: I help my brother: 'Pomagam svojemu ___.'
quiz.explanation: The verb 'pomagati' governs the dative case; masculine singular ending is '-u' (bratu).

quiz.question: Which sentence has the correct clitic order?
quiz.explanation: 'Mu' (dative) comes before 'ga' (accusative), followed by the auxiliary 'je': 'Včeraj mu ga je dal.'

quiz.question: She wrote a letter to Ana: 'Napisala je pismo ___.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in '-a' take '-i' in the dative singular: 'Ani'.

tip: Memorize the clitic sequence acronym: D-A-G (Dative, Accusative, Genitive), with auxiliary verbs coming at the very end of the pronoun group (except 'je', which drops to the end of the entire clitic string).

title: Motion vs. Location Prepositions
subtitle: Distinguish movement toward a destination from remaining in a place
keyPoint: Prepositions like 'v' and 'na' trigger the Accusative case for direction (Kam?) and the Locative case for static location (Kje?).

mistakes.note: Movement toward a goal requires the accusative ending -o, not locative -i.
Being located inside or at an institution uses locative -i with 'na'.
Traveling towards the seaside or coast takes 'na' + accusative.

quiz.question: Kam greš jutri popoldne? — Grem ___.
quiz.explanation: The question 'Kam?' asks for direction, requiring 'v' + accusative neuter (gledališče).

quiz.question: Kje je tvoja sestra? — Ona sedi ___.
quiz.explanation: The question 'Kje?' asks for static location, requiring 'v' + locative feminine (kavarni).

quiz.question: Vsi študenti hitijo ___.
quiz.explanation: Higher education institutions take preposition 'na', and motion takes the accusative (fakulteto).

quiz.question: Kje imaš ključe? — Pozabil sem jih ___.
quiz.explanation: Location on a surface is expressed with 'na' + locative (mizi).

tip: Ask yourself 'Kam?' (movement towards) vs. 'Kje?' (stillness) before deciding between accusative and locative.

title: Definite vs. Indefinite Masculine Adjectives
subtitle: Distinguish specific items from generic ones using -i vs -ø
keyPoint: Masculine nominative adjectives end in a consonant (-ø) when indefinite ('a/an') and in '-i' when definite ('the' or preceded by demonstratives).

examples.en: Ta lepi grad stoji na hribu.
Kateri hotel je dober? Tisti dobri hotel pri postaji.
To je star hrast, tisti stari hrast ima sto let.

mistakes.note: Demonstrative pronouns like 'ta' or 'tisti' require the definite form ending in -i.
When introducing a non-specific item for the first time, use the indefinite form (moder).
Possessive adjectives ending in -ov/-ev or -in never add the definite -i suffix.

quiz.question: Peter ima ___ klobuk.
quiz.explanation: Indefinite introduced item without demonstratives requires the base masculine ending without -i (črn).

quiz.question: Kje je ___ zvezek?
quiz.explanation: Demonstrative 'tisti' marks specificity, requiring the definite ending -i on the adjective (modri).

quiz.question: Poglej tistega gospoda! Kateri gospod? Tisti ___ mož.
quiz.explanation: Answering 'Kateri?' with a demonstrative requires the definite adjective form (visoki).

quiz.question: To je zelo ___ dan.
quiz.explanation: Describing quality in general ('Kakšen?') after 'zelo' takes the indefinite form (prijeten).

tip: If you can translate it with 'the' or pair it with 'ta' (this), add -i; if it translates to 'a/an', leave it bare.

title: Verbal Aspect: Perfective vs. Imperfective
subtitle: Distinguish finished actions from ongoing processes and habits
keyPoint: Imperfective verbs express ongoing, habitual, or repeated actions, while perfective verbs view an action as completed as a single whole.

useCases.label: Ongoing Process Right Now
useCases.example: Dve uri že berem to knjigo.

examples.en: Cel večer sem pisal pismo prijatelju.
Ob polnoči sem pismo končno napisal.
Vsak dan kupujem kruh v isti pekarni.
Ura bije, medtem ko se pogovarjava.

mistakes.wrong: Jutri bom napisal pismo dve uri.
mistakes.right: Jutri bom pisal pismo dve uri.
mistakes.note: Expressions of continuous duration ('dve uri') require the imperfective aspect.
Phase verbs like začeti, nehati, and nadaljevati only combine with imperfective infinitives.
Present forms of perfective verbs cannot express an action happening at this exact moment.

quiz.question: Vsako soboto ___ stanovanje.
quiz.explanation: 'Vsako soboto' indicates a recurring habit, demanding an imperfective present verb (pospravljam).

quiz.question: Ali lahko prosim ___ to okno?
quiz.explanation: A polite request for a single complete action uses the perfective form (zapreš).

quiz.question: Učenec je končno ___ vsa vprašanja.
quiz.explanation: The word 'končno' indicates reaching a completed result, requiring the perfective past form (odgovoril na).

quiz.question: Takoj ko sem končal delo, sem ___ film.
quiz.explanation: Completion of a single sequential action in the past requires the perfective verb (pogledal).

tip: Use imperfective with time spans (dve uri, cel dan) and perfective with time points or results (ob petih, končno).

title: Supine vs. Infinitive
subtitle: Master the shortened verb form used after verbs of movement
keyPoint: The supine (namenilnik) drops the final '-i' (-t/-č) and is used exclusively directly after verbs expressing directional movement.

examples.en: Rada bi se naučila dobro plavati.
Oče je šel v klet iskat orodje.
Prišel sem te obiskat za kratek čas.
Zvečer moram brati, čeprav bi raje šel gledat film.

mistakes.note: After verbs of movement like 'iti', the supine 'spat' must be used instead of infinitive 'spati'.
After modal verbs like 'morati', Slovenian standard grammar requires the infinitive 'delati'.
For -či verbs after a motion verb, the supine drops the final vowel, becoming -č (teč).

quiz.question: Zvečer gremo v kino ___ novo dramo.
quiz.explanation: Following the motion verb 'gremo', the purpose requires the supine ending -t (gledat).

quiz.question: Danes moram resno ___ za izpit.
quiz.explanation: Modal verb 'moram' requires the full infinitive ending in -ti (študirati), not the supine.

quiz.question: Mama je tekla v kuhinjo ___ večerjo.
quiz.explanation: The motion verb 'tekla je' demands the supine form ending in -t (kuhat).

quiz.question: Ali znaš dobro ___ kruh?
quiz.explanation: Modal verb 'znati' takes the infinitive ending in -či (peči), not the supine form.

tip: Remember: Movement = Short (-t/-č). Modal & General = Long (-ti/-či).

title: Present and Past Conditional with 'bi'
subtitle: Form polite requests, hypothetical scenarios, and counterfactuals
keyPoint: The conditional mood uses the uninflected particle 'bi' paired with the past active -l participle across all persons and genders.

cells: I would have helped back then.
Če bi imel denar, bi potoval.
If I had money, I would travel.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Condition
useCases.example: Če bi imel čas, bi šel v gore.

useCases.label: Unreal Past Counterfactual
useCases.example: Če bi bil vedel, bi prišel.

examples.en: Ali bi mi podal sol, prosim?
Če bi sijalo sonce, bi plavali v jezeru.
Brez tvoje pomoči ne bi uspeli.
Včeraj bi bila ostala doma, če bi bila bolna.

mistakes.wrong: Jaz bom hotel kavo. (for polite ordering)
mistakes.note: In Slovenian, express polite wishes with 'bi' + adjective 'rad', not the future tense of want.

mistakes.wrong: Če bom imel čas, bi prišel.
mistakes.right: Če bi imel čas, bi prišel.
mistakes.note: Hypothetical conditions must have 'bi' in both the 'če' condition clause and the result clause.
The particle 'bi' never declines in Slovenian (*bomo, *bite, *bimo do not exist in the conditional).

quiz.question: Ali ___ z mano skodelico čaja?
quiz.explanation: A polite offer uses the invariable particle 'bi' + the masculine l-participle (bi popil).

quiz.question: Če bi imeli več časa, ___ se nov jezik.
quiz.explanation: Both clauses in hypothetical conditionals require 'bi'; 'bi se učili' matches the plural subject.

quiz.question: Ona ___ se rada zahvalila za prijaznost.
quiz.explanation: The invariable conditional particle 'bi' is used for all genders and persons with 'rad/rada'.

quiz.question: Če bi včeraj deževalo, ___ doma.
quiz.explanation: Past conditional takes 'bi' followed by the auxiliary 'bili' and participle 'ostali'.

tip: Unlike other Slavic languages, Slovenian 'bi' never inflects: jaz bi, ti bi, on bi, mi bi, vi bi, oni bi all use identical 'bi'!

title: Complex Clitic Climbing in Multi-Clause Sentences
subtitle: Mastering the placement of pronoun and auxiliary clusters in complex verb phrases
keyPoint: In Slovenian, clitics generally climb to the second position of the matrix clause when governed by modal or aspectual verbs, adhering strictly to the Wackernagel position.

cells: Včeraj sem se mu moral opravičiti.
Yesterday I had to apologize to him.
I started reading him the book.
Vem, da se mu nočeš zlagati.
I know that you don't want to lie to him.

useCases.label: Modal Auxiliary Climbing
useCases.example: Včeraj sem se mu moral predstaviti.

useCases.label: Aspectual Verbs with Clitics
useCases.example: Takoj sem mu jo začel razlagati.

useCases.label: Subordinate Conjunction Anchor
useCases.example: Mislim, da se mu bo hotel zahvaliti.

examples.en: Včeraj sem se mu moral opravičiti za zamudo.
Ali bi mi jo lahko posodil za en teden?
Nisem se mu hotel zlagati o rezultatih.
To zgodbo sem mu že včeraj hotel povedati.
Povedal je, da se mu ne more javiti.

mistakes.note: Clitics should not trail after the infinitive at the end of the clause in standard Slovenian.

mistakes.wrong: Včeraj sem mu se hotel zahvaliti.
mistakes.right: Včeraj sem se mu hotel zahvaliti.
mistakes.note: The reflexive particle 'se' must precede personal pronoun clitics like 'mu'.
The auxiliary clitic 'sem' precedes the pronominal clitic 'ga'.

quiz.question: Včeraj ___ hotel predstaviti celotni ekipi.
quiz.explanation: The required order is auxiliary (sem) + reflexive (se) + dative pronoun (mu).

quiz.question: Ali ___ lahko posodiš svoj svinčnik?
quiz.explanation: Dative clitics (mi) always precede accusative clitics (ga).

quiz.question: Mislim, da ___ hotel pomagati pri nalogi.
quiz.explanation: 'Ti je' correctly places the dative pronoun before the 3rd person auxiliary 'je'.

quiz.question: Zvečer ___ moral vrniti sposojeno knjigo.
quiz.explanation: The future auxiliary 'bom' comes before the dative clitic 'mu'.

tip: Remember the golden cluster order: Auxiliary (except 3rd person 'je') -> Reflexive 'se' -> Dative -> Accusative/Genitive -> 'je'.

title: Relative Clauses: 'ki' with Clitics vs. 'kateri'
subtitle: Navigating indeclinable 'ki' with resumptive clitics versus prepositional 'kateri'
keyPoint: Use indeclinable 'ki' accompanied by a resumptive clitic pronoun for bare cases, but switch to declined forms of 'kateri' whenever a preposition is required.

cells: Prijatelj, o katerem govorim, živi v Celju.
To je študent, ki bere knjigo.
Film, ki sem ga gledal, je odličen.
Človek, ki sem mu pomagal, je bil hvaležen.

useCases.label: Subject Relative Clause
useCases.example: Dekle, ki sedi tam, je moja sošolka.

useCases.label: Object Relative Clause with Clitic
useCases.example: Avto, ki ga je kupil, je zelo hiter.

useCases.label: Prepositional Relative Clause
useCases.example: Mesto, v katerem sem odraščal, je majhno.

examples.en: To je knjiga, ki sem jo prebral v enem dnevu.
Gospod, o katerem sva se pogovarjala, je prispel.
Zdravnik, ki mu zaupam, dela v Mariboru.
Miza, na kateri ležijo ključi, je lesena.
To so ljudje, ki so nam priskočili na pomoč.

mistakes.wrong: To je človek, o ki sem ti govoril.
mistakes.right: To je človek, o katerem sem ti govoril.
mistakes.note: 'Ki' cannot follow a preposition; you must use the declined form of 'kateri'.

mistakes.wrong: Knjiga, katero sem jo prebral, je dobra.
mistakes.right: Knjiga, ki sem jo prebral, je dobra.
mistakes.note: Do not double 'katero' with a resumptive clitic pronoun ('jo').

mistakes.wrong: To je prijatelj, ki sem videl včeraj.
mistakes.right: To je prijatelj, ki sem ga videl včeraj.
mistakes.note: When 'ki' marks a non-subject oblique argument, a resumptive clitic pronoun (here 'ga') is obligatory.

quiz.question: To je avto, ___ je moj oče kupil pred enim tednom.
quiz.explanation: 'Avto' is the direct object of 'kupil', requiring 'ki' with the masculine accusative clitic 'ga'.

quiz.question: Kje je hiša, v ___ si preživel otroštvo?
quiz.explanation: 'Hiša' is feminine, so preposition 'v' + locative requires feminine singular 'kateri'.

quiz.question: Prijateljica, ___ sem posodil zvezek, je bila vesela.
quiz.explanation: 'Prijateljica' is the indirect dative object of 'posodil', requiring 'ki ji'.

quiz.question: Spoznal sem fanta, ___ tekoče govori pet jezikov.
quiz.explanation: The relative pronoun stands as the subject (nominative), so bare 'ki' without a clitic is required.

tip: A simple rule of thumb: If there is a preposition directly preceding the relative pronoun, you must decline 'kateri'; otherwise, use 'ki' plus an appropriate clitic.

title: Adverbial Participles (Deležja in -oč/-eč, -ši)
subtitle: Forming and applying present and past adverbial participles in formal prose
keyPoint: Present adverbial participles (-oč/-eč) express simultaneous action with imperfective verbs, while past adverbial participles (-vši/-ši) denote prior completed action with perfective verbs.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Action (Present)
useCases.example: Sedel je v kotu, tiho prebirajoč pismo.

useCases.label: Subject State While Acting
useCases.example: Ne vedoč za nevarnost, je stopil naprej.

examples.en: Hodila sta po parku, držéč se za roke.
Odprl je vrata, rekoč nekaj nerazumljivega.
Spil je čaj, čakajoč na naslednji vlak.
Slišavši novico, je nemudoma poklical mamo.
Pogledal jo je, ne vedoč, kaj naj odgovori.

mistakes.right: Ko je prebral knjigo, je telefon zazvonil.
mistakes.note: Dangling participle: the implicit subject of an adverbial participle must be identical to the subject of the main clause.
Use the past participle (-vši) from perfective verbs for an action completed before the main verb.
Deležja cannot function as periphrastic progressive tense predicates; use finite verbs instead.

quiz.question: Dekle je odšlo iz sobe, ___ solze.
quiz.explanation: The action is simultaneous and uses an imperfective verb stem: 'skrivati' becomes 'skrivajoč'.

quiz.question: ___ pismo, ga je takoj vrgel v ogenj.
quiz.explanation: The action of reading was fully completed prior to burning the letter, requiring perfective past 'prebravši'.

quiz.question: Mati je kuhala kosilo, ___ svojo najljubšo pesem.
quiz.explanation: 'Pojoč' (from 'peti') represents simultaneous ongoing singing while cooking.

quiz.question: Starinec je stal pri oknu, ___ v daljavo.
quiz.explanation: 'Strmeč' is the present adverbial participle of 'strmeti' denoting an ongoing simultaneous state.

tip: Adverbial participles do not decline for gender, number, or case. They are invariant adverbs and strictly share their subject with the main clause.

title: Morphological Passive vs. Impersonal 'se' Constructions
subtitle: Distinguishing periphrastic passives ('biti' + participle) from reflexive-impersonal syntax
keyPoint: Periphrastic passives emphasize the resulting state of a patient, whereas reflexive-impersonal 'se' constructions describe an action or general practice without specifying an agent.

cells: The house was built last year.
V tej hiši se je dobro spalo.
One slept well in this house.

useCases.label: Periphrastic Resultative Passive
useCases.example: Most je bil zgrajen pred stotimi leti.

examples.en: Vsa naročila so bila poslana pravočasno.
V tej restavraciji se dobro je.
Projekt bo zaključen do konca meseca.
O tem vprašanju se je veliko razpravljalo.

mistakes.note: In reflexive passive constructions, the verb agrees in number and gender with the nominative subject ('knjige' is plural nominative).

mistakes.wrong: Avto je bil opran od očeta.
mistakes.note: Expressing an explicit animate agent with 'od' + genitive is unidiomatic in Slovenian; use an active clause instead.

mistakes.wrong: Se je delalo celo noč od delavcev.
mistakes.note: Impersonal 'se' constructs cannot take an agentive phrase; use active voice when naming who acted.

quiz.question: Nova šola ___ leta 2020.
quiz.explanation: A completed periphrastic passive state requires the auxiliary and the passive -n/-t participle: 'je bila zgrajena'.

quiz.question: V tem laboratoriju ___ strogi varnostni predpisi.
quiz.explanation: 'Predpisi' is nominative plural, so the reflexive passive verb must agree in plural: 'se upoštevajo'.

quiz.question: O tem predlogu ___ še včeraj.
quiz.explanation: Intransitive impersonal actions take 3rd person neuter singular with 'se': 'se je razpravljalo'.

quiz.question: Vstop v stavbo brez dovolilnice ___ strogo prepovedan.
quiz.explanation: 'Je prepovedan' is the standard periphrastic predicate ('biti' + participle 'prepovedan').

tip: If the agent is known and important, always prefer the active voice in Slovenian; reserve 'biti + deležnik' for completed states and 'se' for true agentless generalities.

title: Complex Quantificational Genitive and Numeral Syntax
subtitle: Navigating case shifts and agreement across paucal numbers and quantifiers
keyPoint: Numerals 5 and above govern the genitive plural and require neuter singular predicate agreement, whereas numerals 2, 3, and 4 preserve paucal cases and dual/plural verb agreement.

useCases.label: Indefinite Quantity (Veliko, Malo)
useCases.example: Veliko vode je preteklo od takrat.

examples.en: Šest prijateljev je prispelo na zabavo.
Dva nova študenta sta se vpisala na tečaj.
examples.highlight: Dva nova študenta sta se vpisala

examples.en: Tri mačke so spale na toplem soncu.
Na trgu je bilo veliko radovednih turistov.
Zmanjkalo nam je časa za zadnjo nalogo.

mistakes.wrong: Pet fantje so prišli na obisk.
mistakes.right: Pet fantov je prišlo na obisk.
mistakes.note: Numerals from 5 onwards govern the genitive plural ('fantov') and require neuter singular verb agreement ('je prišlo').

mistakes.wrong: Dva psa sta tekla, ampak tri psa so lajala.
mistakes.right: Dva psa sta tekla, ampak trije psi so lajali.
mistakes.note: Number 3 takes nominative plural forms ('trije psi so lajali'), whereas 2 takes dual forms ('dva psa sta tekla').

mistakes.wrong: Veliko ljudi so bili na koncertu.
mistakes.right: Veliko ljudi je bilo na koncertu.
mistakes.note: Indefinite quantifiers such as 'veliko', 'malo', and 'nekaj' govern neuter singular predicate agreement.

quiz.question: Na postaji ___ osem potnikov.
quiz.explanation: Cardinals 5 and higher govern genitive plural ('potnikov') and neuter singular verb agreement ('je čakalo').

quiz.question: V sobo ___ trije visoki fantje.
quiz.explanation: 'Trije fantje' is masculine nominative plural, requiring plural verb agreement ('so vstopili').

quiz.question: V mestnem parku ___ dva stara hrasta.
quiz.explanation: 'Dva stara hrasta' is masculine dual, demanding the dual auxiliary and dual participle 'sta rastla'.

quiz.question: Včeraj ___ veliko nepričakovanih težav.
quiz.explanation: 'Veliko' governs neuter singular agreement in compound tenses: 'se je pojavilo'.

tip: Think of 5+ and indefinite quantifiers like 'veliko' as singular mass containers grammatically: the verb always defaults to the neuter singular 3rd person.
